propositions: The reconciler unconditionally advances its cursor to the newest event in a fetched window, permanently dropping any candidate that failed to receive a vote in that pass (reconcile_check_error, review_timeout, or voter error/deferred)

A patch-set upload event is dropped when the reconciler's cursor reaches the event's timestamp via ?t1= server-side inclusive lower bound filtering, making the event unreachable in all future reconciler passes

The webhook delivery mechanism is at-most-once, not at-least-once: Gerrit webhooks plugin discards events after maxTries with no dead-letter; the receiver 202-ACKs into a volatile asyncio.Queue that is destroyed on container recreation

Three acceptance criteria require the reconciler to re-drive abandoned candidates on subsequent passes, re-expose queue depth and held-back events via /health and reconcile_done, and enforce a bounded holdback window—all failing before the fix due to the cursor mechanism

The guarding test test_deferred_change_stays_eligible_for_reconciler passes falsely because the test double records the since parameter but ignores it, never exercising the production cursor filter on multi-event windows

Two distinct manual nudges (recheck-review comment and no-op rebase) temporarily revive a stalled change by minting new events with timestamps after the persisted cursor, proving the review is dropped rather than queued
